statement_blocker: The catalog supplies only the hp finite-element method label and the mechanisms h-refinement and p-enrichment. It selects no PDE or approximation problem, domain, boundary conditions, variational spaces, mesh/refinement family, polynomial-degree family, regularity regime, hp coupling, norms, constants, ordered binders, or conclusion. Choosing quasi-optimality, an algebraic or exponential error estimate, corner-singularity approximation, or adaptive-hp convergence would invent or substitute proposition-changing mathematics.
target_decision: redirect the method label to a corrected, independently reviewed, immutable exact proposition before ordinary statement or proof execution
domain_and_universes: Open: an admitted source must fix the PDE or approximation problem, scalar field, spatial dimension, domain and boundary, solution and data spaces, meshes and refinements, finite elements, polynomial degree assignments, norms, indices, and exact or computational semantics.
conclusion: Open: the repository does not choose density or best approximation, discrete solvability, quasi-optimality, an a priori hp error estimate, algebraic or exponential convergence, singular-solution approximation, complexity, or adaptive-hp optimality.
degenerate_case_status: No case is excluded before a proposition is selected; statement review must resolve every case listed in scope-map.md.
candidate_scope_not_credited: an hp best-approximation or interpolation bound for a source-selected Sobolev or weighted analytic class
a quasi-optimal discrete variational solution combined with an hp approximation estimate
algebraic convergence on a quasiuniform mesh with uniform polynomial degree
exponential convergence on a geometrically graded mesh for analytic or singular data
convergence or complexity of a source-selected adaptive hp strategy
excluded_substitutions: generic finite-element, Galerkin, Lax-Milgram, or orthogonal-projection theory without an hp discretization and source-selected conclusion
an h-only, p-only, spectral-element, or adaptive-FEM theorem substituted for a combined hp claim
a univariate polynomial-degree inclusion substituted for mesh-indexed conforming finite-element enrichment
mesh generation, degree bookkeeping, matrix assembly, numerical experiments, or empirical convergence
a structure storing the desired solution, estimate, or convergence result as an input
the catalog's untrusted verified label or a successful adjacent-API probe
